name: Jellyfin Federation
description: Aggregate content from multiple Jellyfin servers into unified virtual libraries
overview: The Jellyfin Federation Plugin allows you to create a unified media library by aggregating content from multiple remote Jellyfin servers. Stream content from any server without file synchronization.
changelog: Four additions, no forced item recreation this time (existing watch progress and ids are untouched): (1) Duplicate detection against locally-owned content now checks the whole server, not just the federated library's own folder - a movie you already own in a separate, ordinary library now correctly blocks its federated duplicate from being created. (2) A small icon now appears next to federated items' titles in jellyfin-web (grid cards, lists, and the detail page), so it's clear at a glance which items are streamed from another server - implemented by injecting a small script into index.html at server startup, the same technique other Jellyfin plugins use for client-side additions. (3) Investigated why federated items never showed up in Continue Watching: they already have everything Jellyfin's resume logic needs (stable id, RunTimeTicks, IsVirtualItem=false) - the real cause was that every forced-recreation migration through 0.0.31 wiped saved watch position along with the item it recreated. 0.0.31 was the last of those; resume should now accumulate and persist normally going forward. (4) New optional per-server 'WAN bitrate cap' setting for Direct mode: when the two servers are connected only over the internet (not the same local network), Direct mode previously pulled the source's raw, untranscoded file across that link before transcoding it locally - for a 25+ Mbps 4K HDR release, that can exceed the remote server's own upload bandwidth and cause stuttering that looks like a receiving-server performance problem but isn't. Setting a bitrate cap makes the remote transcode down to a WAN-friendly rate (e.g. 12 Mbps, optionally capping resolution too) before the receiving server ever pulls a byte, at the cost of a second transcode pass. Off by default, unchanged behavior unless set.
